name: Counter is actually advanced inside the loop body vs. counter merely referenced/used inside the loop
side_a: Give the point (no_deduct) when the loop body contains a statement that actually changes the counter's value on each iteration (`suffix++`, `intCounter++` plus re-conversion, etc.), regardless of whether the surrounding loop condition, initial suffix value, or username assignment is correct.
side_b: Deduct when the counter is only read/concatenated inside the loop and is never advanced there (the loop body rebuilds the candidate from the same, unchanged counter value), even though a counter variable exists and is declared/initialized outside the loop.

name: username assigned the loop-verified available candidate vs assigned a value never confirmed available
side_a: No deduct if the field is finally set (outside/after the search) to exactly the string whose availability the loop condition confirmed — i.e., the loop runs `while (!isAvailable(candidate))` and the post-loop assignment uses that same `candidate`.
side_b: Deduct if the value stored in `username` was never confirmed available — e.g., the assignment happens inside the loop to the already-rejected `requestedName`, or the loop exits as soon as the name is *unavailable* so the stored candidate is the failing one (or nothing is stored on some path).

name: numeric suffix search begins at 1 vs begins at 0
side_a: No deduct if the first appended number tried is 1 (e.g., `String counter = "1";` or `int suffix = 1;` used to build the first candidate).
side_b: Deduct if the first appended number tried is 0 (or any value other than 1), so the smallest tested suffix is wrong even though the rest of the loop is correct.
